item.title: UAE denies Israeli reports it struck Iranian desalination plant
item.description: Multiple Israeli media outlets reported Sunday that the United Arab Emirates carried out its first offensive strike against Iran, targeting a desalination facility — a claim the UAE swiftly and categorically denied, calling the reports "fake news" and "inappropriate."

item.title: US, Israel weigh special forces raid to seize Iran's enriched uranium
item.description: The United States and Israel have discussed sending special forces into Iran to secure its stockpile of highly enriched uranium at a later stage of the ongoing war, Axios reported Saturday, citing four sources with knowledge of the discussions. The operation, one of the most sensitive options under consideration, would require American or Israeli troops to enter heavily fortified underground nuclear facilities on Iranian soil.

item.title: Russia says it intercepted 170 Ukrainian drones in four hours
item.description:
Russia's Defense Ministry said on Sunday that its air defense units intercepted 170 Ukrainian drones over central and southern Russia within a four-hour window, in what officials described as a higher-than-average wave of aerial attacks that included two drones headed for Moscow.

The interceptions took place between 2 p.m. and 6 p.m. Moscow time (1100-1500 GMT), according to the ministry. The Bryansk region, which borders Ukraine, recorded the highest concentration with 73 drones intercepted. No damage or casualties were reported.

item.title: Israel says it killed Iran's new military bureau chief in Tehran strike
item.description: The Israeli military announced Sunday that it killed Abu al-Qassem Baba'iyan, the newly appointed head of the military bureau of Iran's supreme leader, in a precision airstrike in Tehran on Saturday. The strike represents the latest in a systematic Israeli campaign to dismantle Iran's senior military command structure since the start of hostilities on February 28.

item.title: Iran threatens to strike regional oil sites after Israel hits Tehran fuel depots
item.description: Iran's military command threatened on Sunday to strike oil facilities across the Middle East if Israel continues its attacks on the Islamic Republic's energy infrastructure, warning that oil prices could surge above $200 per barrel. The threat came as Tehran residents woke to skies choked with toxic black smoke and acidic rainfall after Israeli warplanes hit multiple fuel depots in and around the Iranian capital overnight.

item.title: Israel strikes Tehran oil sites as Trump demands Iran's surrender
item.description: On February 28, 2026, the United States and Israel launched a coordinated military assault on Iran that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and dozens of senior military and political officials, plunging the Middle East into its most volatile conflict in decades. Now entering its ninth day, the campaign — dubbed Operation Epic Fury by the U.S. and Operation Roaring Lion by Israel — has reshaped the region's security landscape with no end in sight.

item.title: Toxic black rain blankets Tehran after Israeli strikes on oil depots
item.description:
Tehran awoke Sunday morning to an apocalyptic scene: thick black clouds blocking out the sun and oil-saturated rain falling across Iran's capital after Israeli airstrikes destroyed multiple fuel storage facilities overnight. The Iranian Red Crescent issued urgent warnings to the city's residents, saying the fires had released "significant quantities of toxic hydrocarbon compounds, sulfur, and nitrogen oxides" into the atmosphere.

"In the event of precipitation, the resulting rain is extremely dangerous and highly acidic," the Red Crescent said in a statement, warning that exposure could cause skin burns and severe lung damage.

item.title: Trump rebuffs UK carrier readiness, says US 'already won' Iran war
item.description:
President Donald Trump publicly dismissed Britain's move to ready its aircraft carrier for possible deployment to the Middle East on Saturday, declaring the United States has "already won" its war with Iran and does not need belated help from its closest ally.

"The United Kingdom, our once Great Ally, maybe the Greatest of them all, is finally giving serious thought to sending two aircraft carriers to the Middle East," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "That's OK, Prime Minister Starmer, we don't need them any longer — But we will remember. We don't need people that join Wars after we've already won!"

The broadside came shortly after the UK Ministry of Defence announced it had halved the deployment readiness window for HMS Prince of Wales, the Royal Navy's flagship carrier, from 10 days to five, according to Sky News. A British official said no final decision had been made on sending the carrier to the region.

item.title: Apple's 50th anniversary kicks off with museum exhibit, new book
item.description: As April 1 draws near, Apple is preparing to mark a half-century since Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne founded Apple Computer Company in a Los Altos, California, garage in 1976. The milestone has prompted an unusual wave of reflection from a company long known for looking forward rather than back.

item.title: Iran reaffirms military alliance with Russia as war intensifies
item.description:
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Sunday dismissed growing international calls for a ceasefire in the country's widening war with the United States and Israel, declaring Tehran will keep fighting until it secures a lasting end to hostilities. The remarks, made during an appearance on NBC's "Meet the Press," came as the conflict entered its second week with no signs of abating and Iran moved closer to naming a successor to the slain Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

"There should be a permanent end of the war. And unless we get to that, I think we need to continue fighting for the sake of our people and our security," Araghchi said. He directly rejected President Trump's demand for Iran's unconditional surrender, drawing a comparison to last year's 12-day conflict with Israel. "We resisted, and after 12 days the Israelis asked for an unconditional ceasefire. So we never give up. We never surrender".

item.title: Iran names Mojtaba Khamenei as new supreme leader
item.description: Iran's Assembly of Experts has selected Mojtaba Khamenei, the 56-year-old son of the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as the country's new Supreme Leader, according to Reuters and Iranian state media reports on Sunday. The appointment marks the first hereditary transfer of power in the Islamic Republic's history — a system founded in 1979 on the explicit rejection of monarchy.

item.title: Iran war widens as Bahrain reports desalination plant struck, Saudi Arabia sees first deaths
item.description: The war between Iran and a U.S.-Israeli coalition widened into attacks on civilian infrastructure on Sunday as Bahrain accused Iran of striking a desalination plant and Saudi Arabia reported its first fatalities in the nine-day-old conflict.

item.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine recaptured up to 435 sq km in south
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced on March 8 that Ukrainian defense forces have recaptured between 400 and 435 square kilometers of territory in southern Ukraine over the past six weeks, calling the campaign a success in disrupting Russian military plans in the region.

item.title: Iran war hits civilian infrastructure as Mojtaba Khamenei named supreme leader
item.description: The nine-day-old war between the U.S.-Israeli coalition and Iran widened into civilian infrastructure on Sunday as both sides struck energy and water facilities, while Iranian state television announced that Mojtaba Khamenei has been named the country's new supreme leader, succeeding his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in the opening strikes of the conflict on February 28.

item.title: Energy Secretary Wright says Hormuz tanker traffic could resume within weeks
item.description:
U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Sunday that an oil tanker had successfully passed through the Strait of Hormuz, offering the first glimmer of hope that the critical waterway could resume regular shipping after being effectively shut down for nearly a week following U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran.

"We're not too long away, I think, before you'll see more regular resumption of ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz," Wright said on CNN's "State of the Union," adding that in a "worst case" scenario, full resumption could take "a few weeks, that's not months."

item.title: Yardeni raises market meltdown odds to 35% as Iran war widens
item.description:
Veteran Wall Street strategist Ed Yardeni has sharply raised the probability of a market meltdown to 35% for the remainder of 2026, up from 20%, as the escalating war in Iran threatens to upend global energy markets and drag the U.S. economy toward stagflation. In what he described as "fast-moving times," the president of Yardeni Research also slashed his odds of a market meltup, according to Bloomberg.

The revision marks a dramatic shift for one of Wall Street's most closely watched strategists, who just days earlier had maintained his meltdown estimate at 20% while predicting a "short war" scenario that would see oil prices fall quickly once hostilities ended.

item.title: Video shows US Tomahawk missile hitting near Iran school that killed 175
item.description:
Newly released video footage, authenticated by the investigative outlet Bellingcat, shows a US Tomahawk cruise missile striking an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps naval facility in Minab, Iran, on February 28 — the same location where a girls' elementary school was destroyed, killing at least 175 people, most of them children between the ages of 7 and 12.

The footage, originally released by Iran's Mehr News Agency and geolocated by Bellingcat, also captures smoke already rising from the vicinity of the Shajareh Tayyebeh girls' school at the time the missile hits the adjacent IRGC compound. Bellingcat noted that the United States is the only participant in the conflict known to possess Tomahawk missiles, and that Israel does not operate the weapon. The findings add to a growing body of evidence from The New York Times, CNN, CBC, and NPR suggesting the US military was responsible for the deadliest single strike on civilians since the war began on February 28.

item.title: South Korea, Taiwan cap fuel prices as oil tops $100
item.description: South Korea and Taiwan moved on Monday to impose caps on domestic fuel prices as surging oil costs driven by the expanding conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran ripple through energy-dependent Asian economies.

item.title: Musk pushes vision of robot-powered 'sustainable abundance'
item.description: Elon Musk is doubling down on his vision of a future where artificial intelligence and robots handle all labor, rendering traditional work optional and ushering in an era of what he calls "sustainable abundance." The Tesla CEO's sweeping predictions, repeated across forums from Davos to podcasts in recent months, have drawn both fascination and sharp criticism from economists, politicians, and fellow tech leaders.

item.title: Asian markets plunge as oil tops $100 amid Iran conflict
item.description: A sharp spike in crude oil prices past $100 a barrel sent shockwaves through Asian markets on Monday, with Japanese stocks suffering their steepest single-day decline since April and the Indian rupee sliding to an all-time low as the escalating U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran continued to choke global energy supplies.
